key_insight: Effective resistance in tissue-specific interactomes contains a reproducible, depth-dependent residual signal for graph neural network reliability, even after accounting for degree and other node-level confounders.
engineering_relevance: For protein function annotation, this suggests tissue-specific graph structure can help estimate which GNN predictions to distrust, enabling more reliable selective prediction and uncertainty screening.
method: Analyzed 24 tissue-specific protein interactomes and compared effective resistance against degree and degree-preserving null graphs.
Controlled for predictive entropy, degree, annotation count, local graph structure, and feature-only difficulty while evaluating held-out GNN loss across depths.
Tested whether the residual resistance signal improves reliability estimation beyond baseline controls and permutation floors.
evidence_signal: Across 24 networks, residual effective resistance exceeded degree-preserving null graphs, explained extra held-out per-node loss in 19/24 networks, and its effect grew monotonically with depth.
watch_item: Because effective resistance strongly degenerates toward inverse degree as co-expression filtering increases, its utility may be limited when graph structure is dominated by degree effects or when networks are highly sparse.
paper_title: Effective Resistance and Graph Neural Network Reliability in Tissue-Specific Interactomes
